name: Autodesk EAGLE
version_reference: 9.6.0 (verified against a local 9.6.0 installation, its built-in help and manuals; the last release was 9.6.2)
description: EAGLE (Easily Applicable Graphical Layout Editor) is a schematic capture and printed circuit board design program: a Schematic Editor with multi-sheet and hierarchical designs (modules and ports), a Board Editor with manual, interactive (push-and-shove, differential pair, multi-trace, BGA fan-out), follow-me and automatic routing, a Library Editor for symbols, packages, 3D packages and devices, forward and back annotation that keeps schematic and board consistent, design rule and electrical rule checks, a CAM Processor that writes Gerber RS-274X/X2, Excellon drill, assembly and drawing data from JSON CAM jobs, a built-in SPICE simulator (ngspice) for schematics, and a C-like User Language (ULP) for programs that read and generate design data. Every editor action is a text command (ADD, NET, ROUTE, DRC, CHANGE, SET...), so designs can be scripted with .scr files. Design files (.sch, .brd, .lbr) are plain XML described by eagle.dtd, which makes them easy to read and generate without EAGLE. Status: Autodesk stopped selling and supporting EAGLE on 7 June 2026 and shut down its licensing servers; the editors now stop at the Autodesk 'Sign in' window, while the command-line CAM Processor (eaglecon -X) still produces manufacturing data (checked on 9.6.0 in September 2026). Autodesk Fusion's Electronics workspace is the successor and opens EAGLE files; Altium Designer, OrCAD, KiCad and others import them.

automation.summary: Three entry points. (1) The command-line CAM Processor: eaglecon.exe (the console twin of eagle.exe) with -X runs without the GUI and without signing in; -dCAMJOB -j<job.cam> -o<directory> processes a complete JSON CAM job (Gerber, drill, assembly, drawings) and a legacy device (-dGERBER_RS274X, -dEXCELLON, -dPS, -dEPS, ...) plus a layer list writes one file. (2) Commands and programs inside the editor: '-C "<commands>"' loads a .sch/.brd/.lbr and executes the given editor commands (for example RUN my.ulp; QUIT); scripts (.scr) are sequences of the same commands and ULP programs read the design through objects such as UL_BOARD and UL_SCHEMATIC and can emit commands with exit("..."). Since the licensing shutdown this route needs a working Autodesk sign-in, which automation must never perform. (3) The design files are XML (eagle.dtd): parts, nets, signals, layers, attributes, variants, design rules and libraries can be read and generated directly by any program.

cli.description: Run a complete JSON CAM job headless: Gerber files, Excellon drill, Gerber job file and assembly/pick-and-place outputs are written under the output directory (CAMOutputs\GerberFiles, DrillFiles, Assembly). -N suppresses messages. Verified on 9.6.0 without signing in (about 4 s for a small board).
Legacy single-output mode: device driver from eagle.def plus the layers to include (here Top, Pads, Vias).
Legacy Excellon drill file for the Drills and Holes layers.
Print the version banner ('EAGLE Version 9.6.0') and the option list; -d? lists the legacy output devices defined in eagle.def.
Generate the CAM data for a named assembly variant (-A).

Open a design in the editor and execute commands as if typed into its command line (eagle.scr is not run, -s is ignored, user settings are not written back). Needs the editor, therefore a valid Autodesk sign-in after the June 2026 licensing shutdown.
Start without reading or writing the eaglerc user settings file; -U<file> uses a specific settings file.

apis.name: Editor commands and scripts (.scr)
apis.description: Every editor operation is a command with a text syntax; a script file is a list of commands separated by semicolons, run with SCRIPT file.scr (eagle.scr runs automatically when an editor opens).

apis.name: User Language (ULP)
apis.description: C-like programs run with RUN file.ulp [args]. Builtin statements board(), schematic(), library(), sheet(), module() give access to objects (UL_BOARD, UL_ELEMENT, UL_SIGNAL, UL_SCHEMATIC, UL_PART, UL_NET...); output() writes files, dlg* functions build dialogs, exit("commands") hands commands back to the editor.

apis.name: XML design files
apis.description: Schematics, boards and libraries are XML documents (root <eagle>, sections <drawing><settings/><grid/><layers/> and <schematic>/<board>/<library>) defined by doc/eagle.dtd; any XML reader can extract parts, nets, signals and attributes or generate designs.

file_formats.description: Schematic (XML): libraries used, parts, sheets with instances, nets, busses, attributes, variants, modules.
Board (XML): plain objects, libraries used, elements (placed packages), signals with wires/vias/polygons, design rules and autorouter settings.
Library (XML): packages, 3D packages, symbols and devicesets (gates, devices, connects, technologies).
Script: a sequence of editor commands.
CAM job; JSON since 9.0 (sections for Gerber, drill, drawing, assembly outputs).
Design rules file loaded with DRC LOAD / the DRC dialog.
Project file eagle.epf in a project folder (open windows and settings).
Backup copies of board, schematic and library written on save; .b## .s## .l## are automatic backups.
eagle.def: output device definitions for the legacy CAM and printer drivers.
Aperture wheel and drill rack files for legacy Gerber RS-274D and drill output.
